subject: CloudForge renewal: commit flexibility, price-hold request, and bridge credits
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena.park@cloudforge.com>
To: lukas_meyer@redwood.ai
Cc: samir@cloudforge.com, legal@cloudforge.com
Date: Sat, 20 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal planning / price-hold request for next year

Lukas —

Thanks for the kickoff yesterday. CloudForge is preparing our budget and we'd like to outline one preferred path for renewal so we can present a clean ask to Finance. Two asks up front: a) a 12-month price hold at our current blended rate (we're under a fixed contract this year and can't absorb a large step-up) and b) the ability to move 20% of committed capacity into a "burst buffer" without penalty for the first 90 days after renewal — that buys us time while we finalize an integration.

We are open to structured credits instead of deeper list discounts if that helps keep the unit economics intact on your end. I attached our Q3 usage summary for reference. Would love a quick sketch of options (credits, temporary price hold, or a small uplift with credits) by the end of next week.

Elena
Elena Park
VP Finance, CloudForge
(elena.park@cloudforge.com)

Attachments: CloudForge_Q3_usage_summary.csv

From: lukas_meyer@redwood.ai
To: Elena Park <elena.park@cloudforge.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 22 Nov 2027 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal planning / price-hold request for next year

Elena —

Thanks for the context and the usage file. Appreciate the clarity on what Finance needs. High-level, we can move in three practical directions:

1) Price-hold + limited burst buffer: 12-month price hold at current blended rate + 20% burst buffer for 90 days. To protect our serving capacity, we'd require a 6% committed uplift on baseline for the term (applied as a billing credit schedule).

2) Credit-first approach: Maintain a modest list rate change (3–5% uplift) but issue an upfront bridge credit to neutralize billing impact for the first two quarters. Credits would amortize monthly and be earned against committed usage.

3) Multi-year swap: 24-month commitment with a deeper effective discount and an agreed true-up cadence. This reduces churn risk for both sides but requires an exec sign-off.

I've looped Ben (pricing) and Grace (customer success) to make sure the proposed operational guardrails are acceptable (burst routing, fallbacks to smaller instance types, and monitoring thresholds). Can we set a 30-min call Thursday to align on which path CloudForge prefers? I can circulate a one-pager for each option beforehand.

Best,
Lukas Meyer
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

Attachments: (draft) — will follow term-sheet options

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: lukas_meyer@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 23 Nov 2027 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: CloudForge pricing sketches

Team —

Quick notes on the three options Lukas outlined. High-level economics and operational notes below.

Option 1 (price-hold + 20% burst):
- Risk: potential spike in burst usage during onboarding. Recommend: cap burst throughput with an alert + auto-fallback to a slightly lower-tier CPU instance after 90% of burst consumption.
- Economics: require 6% committed uplift (applied as guaranteed monthly minimum). Equivalent to ~2.8% uplift NRR over the year after amortized credits.

Option 2 (credit-first):
- Better short-term win: a one-time bridge credit equal to ~2 months of current billing. Credits amortize over 6 months.
- This is reversible if usage exceeds thresholds — triggers true-up.

Option 3 (24-month):
- Most favorable for us (reduces churn). Could offer a 7% list discount vs 12-month if they commit to 24 months and a modest EOM true-up window.

Operational: need to document fallback model in the term sheet (routing, cache priming, KV eviction hygiene), and add performance SLO language tied to credits to avoid disputes.

If Luke can get a call with Elena, we should have a simple term sheet and sample amortization table ready. I can mock the annex with the burst-cap policy.

-Ben
Head of Pricing, Redwood Inference

From: Elena Park <elena.park@cloudforge.com>
To: lukas_meyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Samir Iqbal <samir@cloudforge.com>, CloudForge Legal <legal@cloudforge.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Nov 2027 11:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal planning / price-hold request for next year

Lukas / Ben —

Thanks for the options. We ran this past Finance and Legal. Preference is Option 2 (credit-first) with a couple of constraints:

- Bridge credit equal to 2 months of average spend, amortized over 6 months.
- 12-month term with an option to extend to 24 months at renewal pricing aligned to CPI + 0–2% cap (we need predictability).
- Burst buffer: call it a 20% capacity pool for 90 days, but we need a firm SLA that burst will not be throttled unless Redwood issues a high-utilization notice with 72 hours lead time.
- We would like a clause that any forced throttling during the 90-day buffer triggers an additional credit (pro-rated days).

Legal asked that any credit mechanics and the throttling remedy be expressed in an annex. Samir will coordinate with your legal team to draft that annex.

Elena

On Thu, Nov 25, 2027 at 10:03 AM lukas_meyer@redwood.ai wrote:
> Elena —
> 
> Quick follow-up: Ben and Grace are working on the numbers and a short annex for the burst policy. Will send the draft term sheet by EOD.

From: lukas_meyer@redwood.ai
To: Elena Park <elena.park@cloudforge.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, legal@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 30 Nov 2027 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal planning / price-hold request for next year

Elena —

Appreciate the clarity and the preferred path. Quick summary of agreement and next steps so we're aligned before legal drafts:

- Structure agreed (Option 2): 12-month renewal, bridge credit = 2 months of trailing average spend, amortized over 6 months. We will reflect that as a monthly billing credit in the invoice schedule.
- Burst buffer: 20% capacity for 90 days post-renewal. We'll include a high-utilization notice process with 72 hours lead time and an automatic pro-rated credit remedy if throttling occurs during the protected window.
- Extension option: mutual option to extend to 24 months; pricing guardrails will be CPI + 0–2% cap. We'll add clear definition of CPI index and calculation example.
- Operational annex: Ben and I drafted a short Annex A describing routing fallbacks, cache priming responsibilities, and a monitoring playbook (alerts and ownership).

Next steps:
1) I'll circulate the revised term sheet and Annex A (with amortization table and credit accounting) by EOD tomorrow.
2) Your legal can propose redline points; suggest we do a short working call Thurs (30 minutes) to reconcile items.
3) Once redlines are resolved, I'll send a DocuSign for signatures.

I've attached the updated term sheet draft and the usage report you sent. If this captures everything, I'll loop legal for the redline pass.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this up quickly.

Regards,
Lukas Meyer
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

Attachments: CloudForge_Renewal_Term_Sheet_v2.pdf, CloudForge_Q3_usage_summary.csv
